title: The light of the world (John 8:12)
hook: whoever follows me walks not in darkness
tomorrow: The truth shall make you free

segments.voice: Yesterday, the last day of Tabernacles and rivers of living water. Your line was out of his belly.

The Easter Vigil begins in the dark. The church is black. A single fire is lit outside, and from it one tall candle. A deacon carries it in and stops three times, lifting it and singing the same short phrase: the light of Christ. People light their small candles from it, and the light moves back through the church, hand to hand, until the whole building glows. What the candle proclaims goes back to one sentence Jesus spoke in the middle of an old feast of lamps. We're still at the feast of Tabernacles.
screen: `THE EASTER VIGIL IN THE DARK.` → `ONE CANDLE, THEN HUNDREDS.` → `BACK TO TABERNACLES.`

segments.voice: The feast had water, and it also had light. The Jewish sources describe great golden lampstands set up in the temple courts, so tall that young priests climbed ladders to fill them with oil. The wicks were made from the priests' worn-out garments. The old account says there wasn't a courtyard in Jerusalem that didn't shine with their light, and men danced with torches through the night. Jesus is teaching in the treasury, John says, right by that court. And he says, in the Douay-Rheims: "I am the light of the world: he that followeth me, walketh not in darkness, but shall have the light of life." It's the second great I am. Bread is what you need every day; light is what lets you see everything else. Notice the promise. He doesn't say there will be no darkness. He says the one who follows will not walk in it. Following is a walking word: a lamp held up ahead on a dark road. You still have to walk, but you can see where to put your feet. We heard this light at the start of the Gospel: the light shineth in darkness. In Matthew, Jesus turns it around: you are the light of the world. The Church holds both together: Christ is the light, and those who follow him carry it. That's the Easter Vigil in one gesture: one candle, then every hand passing the flame along.
screen: `GOLDEN LAMPS IN THE TEMPLE COURT.` · `THE SECOND GREAT I AM.` · `NOT NO DARK: NOT WALKING IN IT.` · `ONE CANDLE, PASSED ALONG.` · then, large: `THE LIGHT OF THE WORLD.`

segments.voice: Stand by a window or a lamp, or step outside into daylight, and walk slowly toward the light, feeling each step land. Notice how light changes what you see: edges, colors, faces, your own hands. If you pray, hold the line, he that followeth me walketh not in darkness; if not, just walk and notice the light.
Golden lampstands. Set up in the temple courts at the feast of lights, where Jesus said: I am the light of the world. Today's word.
Your line: not in darkness. Enough light for the next step. Day five hundred seven, done.

screen: `DAY 507 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE TRUTH SHALL MAKE YOU FREE.`

howItsDone: At the Easter Vigil Catholics light the paschal candle from a new fire and pass its flame to candles throughout the church, as the deacon sings "the light of Christ" three times.

chat.says: Why does the Easter Vigil start in the dark with just one candle?
options: The candle proclaims Christ, the light of the world; everyone lights theirs from it.
It relights the golden lamps of Tabernacles, which the Church copied for Easter.
It recalls the darkness at the cross, so the people's candles stay unlit.
chat.meaning: Jesus said, I am the light of the world. The Church holds that Christ is the light and his followers carry it, passing the flame along.

Easter Vigil.meaning: the night liturgy before Easter, begun in darkness

deacon.meaning: an ordained minister who carries the candle in

Tabernacles.meaning: the autumn feast of huts, with water and lamps

treasury.meaning: the part of the temple where Jesus was teaching

notes: Tabernacles lamps (golden lampstands, young priests on ladders, wicks from worn priestly garments, every courtyard lit, torch dancing) paraphrased from Mishnah Sukkah 5:2–4. Confirm details.
Whether John 8:12 is set during or just after Tabernacles: John 7:37 is the last day; 7:53–8:11 intervenes. Stated as 'still at the feast'. Confirm.
Easter Vigil: deacon (or priest) sings 'The Light of Christ' three times while processing; people's candles lit after the first or second. Described generally. Confirm.
'The second great I am' follows the count of 6:35 as the first. Confirm.
Audit (10% sample): the hook claimed the Easter Vigil candle rite comes partly from the feast of Tabernacles, which no source supports; it now links only the words of John 8:12 to the rite.
